It is further stated that all the respondents made allegation that the revisionist demanded the dowry in cash or by way of articles but on the other hand, respondent no.2 to 4 accepted that they sent the articles and cash to the revisionist in the form of the dowry to the revisionist.

6. It is further stated that thereafter revisionist gave a complaint on 21.05.2022 to SHO PS Saket and also sent to ACP and DCP concerned on 24.05.2022 but no action was taken against the respondent no.2 to 4.

A complaint was also sent to Commissioner of Delhi Police on 25.05.2022 which was delivered on 27.05.2022 but no action was taken against the respondent no.2 to 4.

It is further stated that thereafter revisionist filed the complaint along with application under section 156(3) Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) before the court which was dismissed by Ld. ACMM on 04.07.2022 and, therefore, the revisionist filed the present revision petition.

8. Disclaiming the averments made in the present revision petition, it is replied on behalf of the respondent no.2 to 4 that the present revision petition deserves to be dismissed at the threshold as the same has been filed with concealment of material facts.

It is reiterated that on the demand of the revisionist and his family members, respondents had given by NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:

sentences.text:
Having heard Ld. Counsel for revisionist namely Sh.
Dinesh Lal and Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 to 4 Sh. Anoop Kumar, I do not find any merit in the present revision petition for the reasons indicated infra.

10. At the outset, for reference the germane extract of the impugned order is reproduced herein under:
"7.

The fundamental averment of the complainant is that the respondents have made categorical admissions in the FIR registered against them under Section 498A IPC that they have paid dowry to the complainant which, prima facie, amounts to admission of commission of an offence under Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961 by them.

However, the complainant has concealed that, in the above said FIR,
the respondents and the complainant's wife have made serious allegations of persistent dowry demand against the complainant and his family members.

Therefore, his repeated NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2024.11.05 16:29:53 +0530 averments in the instant complaint that he never demanded dowry and despite absence of such demands, dowry was given, is unsubstantiated and appears to be an attempt to hoodwink this court.

It is crystal clear that the respondents are aggrieved by the demand of dowry by the complainant and his family members and, therefore, their statements shall not subject such persons to criminal prosecution under the Act by virtue of Section 7(3) of the Act."
11.

It is lucid from the aforesaid observation of Ld. ACMM that the respondents are protected from the criminal prosecution for giving the dowry by virtue of section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
12.

The first substantive ground raised in the present revision petition is that Ld. ACMM has misconstrued the afore- noted section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 as the protection of the same would be extended only to the wife of the revisionist who can be considered as victim and not her other relatives who are respondents no.2 to 4 herein.

This argument is clearly misplaced and misconceived as section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 does not throw any such implication that it is only the bride who would be considered as the victim and that only she would fall under the ambit of section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Ld. ACMM in the impugned order has referred to the judgment of the High Court of Delhi in Pooja Pg No. 5 of 7 NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date: 2024.11.05 16:30:03 +0530 Saxena Vs. State and Anr [2010 (4) JCC 2780] in which paragraph 11 of the said judgment was also referred wherein the court had observed about the petitioner (being the wife in the said case) and her parents being entitled to the protection envisaged under section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

sentences.text: The next substantive ground is that Ld. ACMM has failed to consider that respondent no.3 had transferred an amount of Rs.25000/- and Rs.46500/- on account of dowry in favor of the revisionist which amounts to giving of dowry punishable under section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

This aspect has also been dealt with by Ld. ACMM in the impugned order wherein it has been observed that in the FIR registered against the revisionist under section 498A IPC, the respondents and the wife of the revisionist have made serious allegations of persistent dowry demand against the revisionist and his family members and the repeated averments of the revisionist that he never demanded any dowry are unsubstantiated.
14.

To add to this observation, in my considered view, until the evidence is led by both the parties during the trial, the aspect of whether dowry was demanded or not cannot be effectively adjudicated upon and thus, at this stage, the averment NAVJEET NAVJEET BUDHIRAJ BUDHIRAJ Date:
2024.11.05 Pg No. 6 of 7 16:30:09 +0530 of the revisionist that he never demanded any dowry from the respondents and despite that a sum of Rs.25000/- and Rs.465000/- was transferred in his account would be in the nature of a self serving statement which in itself cannot constitute a ground for negating the protection accorded to the respondents herein under section 7(3) of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

15. In light of the foregoing discussion, there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order,
which would warrant any kind of interference by allowing the present revision petition.
Revision petition accordingly stands dismissed.
Trial court record be sent back to the concerned court before the date fixed.
Revision file be consigned to record room.
PRONOUNCED IN OPEN COURT NAVJEET by
NAVJEET  BUDHIRAJ
